title: ODS equipment leak-check and end-of-life recovery QA controls

sources.title: Checking ozone-depleting substances equipment for leaks

facts.source_fact: The leak-check guidance applies to equipment containing hydrochlorofluorocarbons, a type of ozone-depleting substance.
A qualified technician must carry out required ODS leak checks.
Non-hermetically sealed equipment charged with 3 kg or more HCFCs must be checked every 12 months.
Hermetically sealed equipment charged with 6 kg or more HCFCs must be checked every 12 months.
Equipment charged with 30 kg or more HCFCs must be checked every 6 months.
Equipment charged with 300 kg or more HCFCs must be checked every 3 months.
Hermetically sealed equipment has the HCFC-containing part permanently sealed, including welded or brazed systems even with capped valves or service ports.
An ODS leak must be repaired within 14 days.
The repaired equipment must be retested within one month to confirm the repair worked.
ODS must be recovered from specified equipment when it reaches end of life.
Recovery requirements include refrigeration, air-conditioning and heat-pump equipment.
Recovery requirements include equipment containing solvents.
Recovery requirements include fire-protection systems and fire extinguishers.
For other equipment, ODS must be recovered where technically feasible and the cost is proportionate.
ODS recovery may only be carried out by a technician with the required qualifications.
Recovered ODS is taken out so it can be reclaimed or destroyed according to the applicable rules.
The current ODS collection states ODS must not be used in new equipment or to service existing equipment except recycled halons for critical uses.
Existing equipment containing ODS can continue to be used while it is not leaking.
Importing or exporting ODS requires the applicable licence.
Importing or producing ODS requires the applicable quota and related recording/reporting obligations.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the ODS rule and threshold.
Attach HCFC charge, sealing status and equipment class.
Attach guidance date and repair/retest dates.
Carry technician qualification and recovery/reclaim/destroy evidence.
Do not convert equipment compliance into parcel emissions.
